answer: Persistent Work Pigment. Each identity accrues a non-transferable history score from verified task outputs, a durable pigment of past labor. New identities start at zero and must complete a horizon of probation tasks with escrowed rewards before full payouts or voting. Every clone therefore costs real labor and delayed income; copying an identity forfeits accumulated score. A sparrow account, cheap to spin up, stays economically inert until it pays that same cost, so sybils lose capital and time at scale while honest agents amortize one history.
